senses.gloss: (Af. of אמן; = h. הֶאֱמִין) to credit, trust, confide; to loan on trust; to admit as evidence.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 15:6">Targ. O. Gen. XV, 6</cite>. Targ. ib. XLV, 26; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 115a:24">B. Kam. 115ᵃ</cite> <he>הֵימוּנֵי הֵימְניה</he> he loaned him on trust (without a pawn).
<cite ref="Ketubot 22b:5">Keth. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>הֵמְנוּהָ רבנן כבי תרי</he> the Rabbis declared his evidence as legal as if there had been two witnesses.
<cite ref="Shevuot 41b:2">Shebu. 41ᵇ</cite> <he>לא לדידיה הֵימְנֵיה</he> he did not trust him by himself (without witnesses).
Y. Ber. II, 4ᶜ top לאילין דברישך הֵימְנִית I trusted those (T’fillin) on thy head; a. fr.—Part. pass. מְהֵימַן (= h. נֶאֱמָן) faithful, reliable; credited, admitted as evidence.
<cite ref="Onkelos Numbers 12:7">Targ. Num. XII, 7</cite> (Y. II <cite ref="E00428"><he>הֵימַן</he></cite>); a. fr.—

<cite ref="Shabbat 10b:3">Sabb. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>דמתרגמינן אלהא מְהֵימְנָא</he> for we translate (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 7:9">Deut. VII, 9</cite>) &c. (only the participle being used as a divine attribute, not the abstract noun).—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 5:4:4">Y. Gitt. V, 47ᵃ</cite> [read:] <he>בעי בר נש מיתן כמה ומתקרי׳ מ׳</he> a man would sacrifice any amount in order to be called trustworthy; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Kamma 4:4:5">Y. B. Kam. IV, 4ᵇ</cite> bot. <cite ref="E00428"><he>הימן</he></cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 86b:18">B. Mets. 86ᵇ</cite> <he>לא מהימנא לך</he> (ed. (= <he>מהימן אנא</he>, part. act.) I do not trust thee (Mss. <he>לא הימן ביה</he> he (Abraham) did not rely on him).
